title: The Broker Returns
description:
You went all-in and it worked. Luck or skill — who knows.
Kim Bujang calls again.
'This time it's real. Three times bigger and way more certain than last time.
You made it before. No reason it won't work again, right?'

choices.result_text:
Three days of digging. This one was pure markup.
'Last time was luck — I can't spend it again.' You hung up.
One win doesn't mean the next one is certain.

'No. Last time was enough.'
Kim Bujang went quiet, then hung up.
Greed is expecting luck to repeat itself.

title: Rock Bottom
description:
Two months since you lost everything on that stolen number from the café.
The goshiwon landlord knocked on your door today.
'This month's rent — still outstanding.'

choices.result_text:
Night shifts at a convenience store. ₩9,860 per hour.
Three weeks later you paid the rent.
Back to zero. But — this time you know exactly where you lost it.

You called.
Your mother sent the money without asking questions.
That was the hardest part.

title: The Man Calls
description:
A call from Kim Bujang.
'Hey. I knew you cut the markup — from the start.
That's exactly why I figured you were the right kind of person.
This time there's something real. No broker. Just you and me, direct.'

choices.result_text:
Two hours over coffee.
This deal had no commission, no inflation.
'The ones who verify are the ones who win.' He said.
A real connection — earned.

'I want to build up a bit more first.'
Kim Bujang said 'Call anytime' and hung up.
The door wasn't closed.

title: The Mentor's Message
description:
A message from the man.
'That deal worked out for you, right?
I waited to see what you'd do with it.
I have someone I want to introduce you to. My person. You can trust them.'

choices.result_text:
The introduction was to a tax accountant.
'Let me show you how to do this cleanly.'
After that, the investment structure changed.
Starting honestly — that's what got you here.

choices.text: Still too early — want to learn more
choices.result_text:
'I appreciate it, but I want to study a bit more first.'
He said 'No rush.'
Not delaying opportunity — just not using it before you're ready.

title: A Year and a Half Later
description:
'Not ready yet. I'll contact you once I've learned more.'
That's what you said.
Today that number called. After a year and a half.
'Still studying?'

choices.result_text:
'...You're here.'
He laughed briefly.
'Someone who knew to say not yet — when they show up, they're actually ready.'
What he handed over that day was the most solid thing you'd ever received.

choices.text: "Thank you, but I've been doing it on my own now."
choices.result_text:
'That works too.'
He hung up.
You'd learned to stand on your own. That was his gift too.

title: What You Learned That Day
description:
Facing an investment decision, something suddenly came back.
What that man in the Gangnam café said.
'The most expensive thing in a market is something being sold in a hurry.'
This deal in front of you is exactly that.

choices.text: Follow what you learned — walk away
choices.result_text:
You stepped back.
Later you found out it was a classic 'distressed sale' scam.
Keeping your ears open in that café protected millions today.

choices.text: Check more carefully because of what you heard
choices.result_text:
You pulled the registration and compared prices.
You entered at fair value.
The difference between knowing and not knowing shows up in moments like this.

title: Meeting Them Again
description:
At a bus stop, by chance.
The person who bought you an americano in the café.
'Oh, it's you from back then. How have you been?'

choices.result_text:
They run a small restaurant, they said.
'Delivery's been keeping us busy lately.' They smiled.
Just a short conversation — but somehow energizing.
They still seemed like someone who buys coffee for strangers.

choices.text: Just say hi and catch the bus
choices.result_text:
'Hello.' And you got on the bus.
Through the window you could see them. They waved briefly.
Sometimes it helps just knowing people like that exist.

title: Hyeonsu's Second Offer
description:
After winning big on the coin, Hyeonsu contacts you.
'Hey, I've got something even more certain this time.
Last time doubled, right? This one triples. For real.'
That 'for real' is nagging at you.

choices.result_text:
'Once is enough.'
Hyeonsu said 'You're going to regret this.'
A few days later came news the coin halved.
Trusting luck twice was never the right call.

title: Hyeonsu and Me
description:
A month since losing everything on the coin.
A text from Hyeonsu.
'Hey I lost everything too. But I think I found something new for real this time.'
Here we go again.

choices.result_text:
'Both of us lost. This time, please stop.'
Hyeonsu said '...Okay.'
Don't know if I can believe it. But I said what needed saying.

Blocked.
Even getting the messages was draining energy.
I feel bad — but right now, I have to look after myself first.

title: A Text from an Old Colleague
description:
Three months since you quit after having your idea stolen.
A KakaoTalk from a former colleague.
'Hey, just so you know — the team lead has been talking about you. Not good stuff.'

choices.result_text:
You saved the email and messenger logs.
Might never use it. But having it is different from not having it.
Being prepared for when it's needed.

choices.text: Don't let it bother you — already gone
choices.result_text:
You didn't want to spend energy on that person.
But every time a job interview brought up the old job, there was a small tightening in the chest.

title: A Message from a Former Boss
description:
The job you left carefully, with everything wrapped up properly.
Today a message from your former team lead.
'Minjun, would it be okay if I wrote you a reference?
Someone's been asking about you.'

choices.result_text:
How you finish becomes the foundation for coming back.
'Someone who left cleanly' — that phrase became a network.
The way you leave is the way you return.

choices.text: "I'm a bit tied up right now" — politely decline
choices.result_text:
'Sure, let me know another time.'
The relationship wasn't broken.
Not doing it when you have no bandwidth is also the right call.

title: Balance Alert
description:
A month and a half since you impulsively quit.
You open the banking app.
Balance: ₩387,000.
Next month's goshiwon rent: ₩450,000.

choices.result_text:
Convenience store nights, four days a week.
You didn't expect to feel this chased after walking out with so much relief.
But — that job wasn't the answer either.

You sent out twenty applications.
Two interviews lined up.
Desperation sharpened into focus.

title: Payment Due
description:
A year since you took a loan for your father's surgery.
Auto-transfer notification. This month: ₩197,000.
The principal hasn't been touched.

choices.text: Set up an early repayment plan
choices.result_text:
You opened a spreadsheet. Eighteen months to pay it off.
Debt with a plan is different from debt without one.
Your father recovered from the surgery. That was enough.

choices.text: Just pay the interest for now — no bandwidth
choices.result_text:
You paid the interest.
When do I pay the principal.
You know every month you delay, the total interest climbs — but still.

title: Mom's Words
description:
Eight months since you couldn't give the money for your father's surgery.
Your mother called.
'Minjun. We borrowed the surgery money from a relative.
We've paid it all back. You don't have to worry.'
Her voice was strangely flat.

choices.text: "Mom, I'm sorry. I'll pay it back."
choices.result_text:
'It's fine. Just do well — that's everything.'
She hung up.
Couldn't tell if that 'it's fine' was forgiveness or protection.
The only answer is to do well.

choices.text: "...Thank you. I'll definitely pay it back someday."
choices.result_text:
Mom said 'Okay' and hung up.
Someday I really have to pay it back.
Hoping that 'someday' doesn't come too late.

title: Dad's Text
description:
Five months since you emptied your savings for your father's surgery.
A text from Dad.
'Minjun. Dad's really sorry. And thank you.'
This might be the first time Dad ever texted you first.

choices.text: "It's fine, Dad. Of course I would."
choices.result_text:
You sent it and held the phone for a while.
One phrase — 'I'm sorry, and thank you' —
strangely carried the whole day.

Dad picked up.
Not many words were said. From either of you.
But some calls are enough just like that.

title: Dad's Reply
description:
A month since you first said 'Dad, things have been hard lately.'
A text from Dad today.
'Minjun. Thank you for telling me. Dad is here.'

choices.result_text:
You sent it and sat with the phone for a moment.
Those words — 'I'm here' —
strangely got you through the rest of the day.

choices.text: Don't reply — too moved to write anything
choices.result_text:
You couldn't find the words.
Just left the read receipt.
Dad seemed like that was enough.

title: Sangchul's Memory
description:
Third meeting with Im Sangchul.
Sitting down at the gukbap place, he spoke first.
'What you told me last time — about your father getting scammed. I still think about it.'

choices.text: "I think it makes me more careful."
choices.result_text:
Sangchul nodded.
'That carefulness is actually a strength. You're not in a rush.'
That day he made an introduction.
Showing your real self had built real trust.

choices.text: "It's just become a goal now. I don't think about Dad anymore."
choices.result_text:
Sangchul looked at you for a moment, then scooped some broth.
'...That's actually the scarier version, you know.'
You thought about what that meant through the whole meal.
